transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Nina Park (Atlas PM), Miguel Santos (Atlas Head Partnerships), Ravi Kapoor (Atlas Sales Dir), Ellie Wong (Atlas Solutions Architect)

Summary (auto): Quick pipeline review and strategy; focus on two Q3 deals; action items captured.

[00:00:05] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:00:12] Nina Park: Hi -- Nina here from Atlas. Miguel, Ravi and Ellie are on as well.
[00:00:16] Miguel Santos: Hey all.
[00:00:18] Jordan Lee: Great. Samir, Lena with me. Samir, you want to kick us off on the technical asks?
[00:00:25] Samir Patel: Sure, quick agenda: pipeline review across the four joint opps, technical blockers for the two prioritized, confirm hosting preference (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC), and action items.
[00:00:38] Ravi Kapoor: Sounds good. For context, our sellers in EMEA flagged two high-velocity deals: "MediCore" and "Finnova". MediCore is a pilot with 200 agents, Finnova is more strategic, likely Q3 close.
[00:00:52] Jordan Lee: Thanks Ravi. Do you have ACVs or target contract sizes?
[00:00:56] Ravi Kapoor: MediCore ~ $85k ARR if goes to production, Finnova ~ $420k ARR target. The other two are longer tail (proof of value stage).
[00:01:07] Nina Park: Quick note -- MediCore requires data residency in the UK and SOC2 evidence, Finnova is more flexible but wants private network connectivity.
[00:01:17] Samir Patel: Understood. On the security side we can share SOC2 report and our compliance pack. For private connectivity we support VPC peering and private endpoints on Dedicated/Private deployments. If they need on-prem, that's heavier.
[00:01:32] Ellie Wong: For Finnova they'd prefer a dedicated pool behind their VPC and customer-managed KMS. Is that something Redwood supports today?
[00:01:41] Jordan Lee: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS integrations and VPC configurations. For Dedicated we can do VPC peering and network restrictions; there are options depending on their SLO needs and cost tolerance.
[00:01:54] Miguel Santos: Pricing will be the sticking point. Atlas wants a co-sell discount and partner margin. Can you outline typical splits?
[00:02:02] Jordan Lee: We typically offer partner co-sell discounts tiered by ARR and commit. For pilots we can be flexible — standard is 12-18% for partner referrals, can discuss higher on reserved commits. I'll share a deck with ranges.
[00:02:15] Ravi Kapoor: Are there any minimum commit requirements for Dedicated?
[00:02:18] Samir Patel: Yes, Dedicated has minimum reserved capacity — region and GPU type will affect the commit. We can estimate for Finnova after a quick benchmark to determine throughput and latency needs.
[00:02:31] Jordan Lee: Let's run a two-week Atlas-led POC for Finnova to validate latency and throughput. Samir, can we run a benchmark plan?
[00:02:38] Samir Patel: Yep. I'll send the benchmark checklist and infra requirements. We'll need sample prompts, expected qps and p95 latency targets.
[00:02:48] Ellie Wong: Good. We can provide prompts and a subset of anonymized logs. Need to confirm redaction rules.
[00:02:54] Lena Ortiz: We can also provision a partner pilot workspace so Atlas can invite the Finnova sellers and whitelist accounts.
[00:03:01] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks. Let's step through the four deals quickly. First MediCore (UK). Current stage: demo -> pilot. Needs SOC2 and UK data residency. Risk: data residency + procurement timeline.
[00:03:15] Nina Park: Procurement is slow, they insist on UK-only hosting. Atlas has a reseller agreement but we need to confirm hosting options.
[00:03:23] Samir Patel: For UK residency, we can route to our UK region and offer Dedicated capacity if they want more isolation. There's also Redwood Private if they insist on customer-controlled infrastructure.
[00:03:34] Ravi Kapoor: What's typical latency for UK region on hosted?
[00:03:37] Samir Patel: Median p50 is around 80-120ms for our hosted models with expected batch sizes; with Dedicated we usually get lower p95 and more consistent p50. We should bench with MediCore's payload.
[00:03:48] Jordan Lee: Next — Finnova (NA). Stage: scoping, likely to move quickly if POC validates performance. Ask: dedicated pool, customer KMS, higher throughput.
[00:03:58] Ellie Wong: They want to keep tokens local to their VPC and have audit logs forwarded to their SIEM.
[00:04:04] Samir Patel: We support audit log shipping to customer endpoints and can integrate with common SIEMs. We'll include log schema in the security pack.
[00:04:11] Miguel Santos: Competitors could be Anthropic or a homegrown solution from Finnova's platform team. We should highlight reliability and cost-per-query.
[00:04:19] Jordan Lee: Agreed. We'll prepare unit economics comparisons. Samir, can you calculate expected cost per 1k calls for the Finnova config (dedicated + KV cache)?
[00:04:28] Samir Patel: Yes, need their sequence lengths and RPS. If we get sample workload we can model it.
[00:04:33] Nina Park: On co-sell motions: Atlas typically wants a joint exec intro to buyer followed by a technical deep dive. We should align on who runs which part.
[00:04:42] Jordan Lee: Proposed motion: Atlas leads exec intro and commercial negotiation, Redwood runs technical deep dive and POC. Joint customer demo for stakeholders. That tends to land well.
[00:04:53] Ravi Kapoor: For the smaller two opps, what's the go/no-go criteria?
[00:04:57] Jordan Lee: For pilots we usually look for stakeholder readiness, budget, and basic security requirements. If data residency or heavy compliance blocks, may be deprioritized.
[00:05:10] Miguel Santos: Any red flags on Redwood side? SLAs? Uptime?
[00:05:14] Samir Patel: We have SLA tiers for Dedicated customers; hosted API has best-effort but strong SLOs. For enterprise we recommend either Dedicated with reserved capacity or Redwood Private for strict SLAs.
[00:05:26] Nina Park: Partner commercial question: how do lead registration and discounting work? We need a simple doc to share with our sellers.
[00:05:33] Jordan Lee: I'll share the partner playbook excerpt and the co-sell pricing grid. That will cover lead registration, margins, and accepted discount bands.
[00:05:42] Ellie Wong: Technical Q — does Redwood support model variant fallback for capacity shortages? Example: switch to a lower-cost quantized variant automatically?
[00:05:50] Samir Patel: Yes, the smart routing can fallback to compatible variants by policy (cost/latency/region). We'll document how to set the policy for Finnova.
[00:06:00] Jordan Lee: Let's talk timeline: if we kick off POC this week, run two-week benchmark, then a 30-day pilot, we could target a late Q3 close for Finnova. Is that realistic?
[00:06:10] Ravi Kapoor: That's aggressive but doable if procurement moves fast. MediCore procurement risk likely pushes them to Q4.
[00:06:18] Nina Park: Atlas will prioritize Finnova with their field reps. We'll aim to have intros by 2026-07-22.
[00:06:24] Miguel Santos: On the legal side, Finnova's standard contract wants indemnity clauses and data processing addendum. Will Redwood accept standard DPA?
[00:06:33] Lena Ortiz: We have a standard DPA and can support customer-required addenda in many cases; legal redlines can take 2-4 weeks depending on scope.
[00:06:42] Jordan Lee: We'll surface a redline-friendly SOW template for pilots to speed procurement.
[00:06:47] Ellie Wong: For the benchmark, what metrics do you need?
[00:06:50] Samir Patel: We'll need target RPS, typical prompt lengths, desired latency p95, tokenization details, and representative prompts. Also whether deterministic output is required (temperature/beam settings).
[00:07:02] Nina Park: We'll pull that together. Any specific infra on our side? VPC details?
[00:07:06] Samir Patel: For hosted POC, minimal infra, just sample data and network allowlist. For Dedicated/pilot with VPC we need CIDR ranges and contact for peering. We'll include that in the checklist.
[00:07:18] Jordan Lee: Ok quick pulse-check — which two opps do we prioritize? Team?
[00:07:22] Miguel Santos: Finnova (NA) and MediCore (UK) are top. The rest are lower velocity.
[00:07:27] Jordan Lee: Agreed. Focus resources there.
[00:07:31] Ravi Kapoor: One objection we often get: cost versus origin model providers. Buyers ask why not just use the cloud GPUs or open-source stack. How do you position Redwood?
[00:07:42] Jordan Lee: We position Redwood as production-first: predictable SLOs, batching/caching to reduce unit cost, and a single operational interface across hosted/dedicated/private. We also highlight support and SLAs that buyers can't get running an in-house stack quickly.
[00:07:58] Nina Park: Good. We'll coach our sellers on that message.
[00:08:02] Jordan Lee: Any regulatory constraints for MediCore beyond UK residency?
[00:08:06] Ellie Wong: They are healthcare adjacent, so minimal PHI, but they want documented data retention and audit trails.
[00:08:12] Samir Patel: We'll provide the retention and audit logs doc, plus options for log forwarding.
[00:08:18] Jordan Lee: For the pilot SOW, let's standardize the acceptance criteria: throughput, latency, and a basic quality eval on a small prompt set. If we hit those, we move to contract.
[00:08:29] Miguel Santos: Sounds fine. On commercial splits, Atlas expects at least 15% margin to compensate field work.
[00:08:36] Jordan Lee: We'll propose 15% for pipeline-sourced deals and include a higher tier for multi-deal commits. I will confirm in the deck.
[00:08:44] Nina Park: One more note: Atlas' sellers like a short battlecard comparing Redwood vs Anthropic and Cohere. Do you have a one-pager?
[00:08:52] Jordan Lee: Yes, I'll attach a competitor battlecard with the pricing/economics summary.
[00:08:57] Ravi Kapoor: Any notable technical limitations we should call out to customers?
[00:09:01] Samir Patel: If they need extremely low single-digit ms latency for on-device use cases that's not our sweet spot. We excel at high throughput and predictable enterprise workloads. Also, some custom quantization paths require model onboarding.
[00:09:12] Jordan Lee: Moving on — operational checklist for partner success: lead registration, pilot SOW template, technical contact, procurement path. Lena, can you own partner onboarding?
[00:09:22] Lena Ortiz: Yes, I'll own. I'll provision the pilot workspace and share the onboarding checklist.
[00:09:28] Jordan Lee: Great. Any final questions from Atlas?
[00:09:31] Nina Park: Just wanted to confirm timeline again: intros by 7/22, pricing deck by 7/21, pilot workspace by 7/22, benchmarks run the week of 7/26. Is that accurate?
[00:09:41] Jordan Lee: Yes — we'll aim for that.
[00:09:44] Miguel Santos: Good.
[00:09:46] Jordan Lee: Ok, recap of action items...
[00:09:49] Jordan Lee: Jordan to send co-sell pricing deck and partner one-pager by 2026-07-21.
[00:09:55] Samir Patel: Samir to send benchmark checklist and schedule run by 2026-07-23.
[00:09:59] Lena Ortiz: Lena to create partner pilot workspace and invite Atlas team by 2026-07-22.
[00:10:03] Nina Park: Nina to share prioritized joint account list and target contacts by 2026-07-24.
[00:10:07] Jordan Lee: Any blockers on Redwood side?
[00:10:09] Samir Patel: None. We'll need the sample prompts and expected RPS to size Dedicated if they choose that path.
[00:10:16] Ravi Kapoor: We'll get those to you.
[00:10:18] Jordan Lee: Excellent. Let's tentatively schedule a 30-minute exec sync on 2026-07-29 to finalize Q3 close plan. I'll send calendar invite.
[00:10:25] Miguel Santos: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:10:28] Jordan Lee: Thanks team. We'll follow up with the docs.
[00:10:31] [END OF CALL]
